blocks.content: The main objective of TRAI is to provide a fair and transparent environment that promotes a level playing field and facilitates fair competition.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) was established on February 20, 1997, to regulate telecom services in India.
TRAI's primary mandate is to create and sustain conditions for the growth of telecommunications in India in a fair and transparent manner.
The TRAI (Amendment) Act of 2000 led to the creation of the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) to handle adjudicatory functions.
TRAI consists of a Chairperson, up to two whole-time members, and up to two part-time members appointed by the Central Government.
TRAI issues binding directions, orders, and regulations on tariff fixation, quality of service standards, and consumer protection.

rows: Regulation of telecom services, tariff setting, and policy recommendations
Adjudication of disputes and hearing of appeals
Appeals against TRAI orders go to TDSAT
Appeals against TDSAT orders go to the Supreme Court

items: Adjudicatory and dispute resolution powers were separated from TRAI and given to TDSAT through the 2000 Amendment Act.
TRAI's recommendations on service provider licensing terms are advisory and not strictly binding on the Central Government.
Decisions and orders of TDSAT can be challenged directly only in the Supreme Court of India.
